title: A new file is added and brings an occurrence with it
why: The positive control for `new`, and the case that makes the outcome falsifiable at all. Broker/Brand.cs does not exist in revision A and revision B records it in `added_paths` with no copy relation to anything, so no predecessor COULD have lived there - that is a fact about the tree, not a failure to find one. Without a case like this, `new` would only ever be reachable by the route the contract forbids, and freezing the word would mean nothing.

expect.note: the untouched occurrence stays untouched; an arrival elsewhere is not news about it

the file is recorded as added and as a copy of nothing, so there is no place a predecessor could have been. The birth SEEDS a root lineage id: occ-b2 may itself branch next revision, and a branch whose parent has no lineage has nothing to record.

forbid: occ-b2 reported as unresolved - the recorded addition is exactly the evidence unresolved says is missing
occ-b2 reported as new on the strength of finding no predecessor, rather than on the recorded addition
occ-a1 disturbed - it is already accounted for, and a birth elsewhere is not evidence about it
a null lineage_id for the birth - a root with no id cannot be named as a parent later, which is exactly how an occurrence id ends up in a lineage field
